 Gov. Kathy Hochul has announced the opening of two New York State student loan forgiveness programs seeking to assist those in the healthcare and agricultural industry.
 Eligible applicants can submit for the Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program and the Young Farmers Forgiveness Incentive Program until Dec. 16, 2026.
 Officials say the first program is designed to increase the number of qualified nursing and adjunct clinical faculty teaching at state nursing schools.
 Those who qualify can get up to $8,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $40,000.
 Applicants eligible for the second program can receive up to $10,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $50,000.
 Hochul’s administration hopes to help college graduates pursue long-term agricultural careers, reduce the financial burden of their education and encourage them to create and maintain farming operations in the state.
 The programs have drawn praise from both education officials and industry figures.
 “These programs help New Yorkers pursue meaningful careers in two fields that are essential to our state’s future. Whether it’s preparing the next generation of nurses or building a career in agriculture, we’re helping people turn their education into lasting opportunities,” said New York State Higher Education Services Corporation Acting President Doris B. González.
 “The state, under the governor’s leadership, has doubled down on its efforts to support the next generation of New York’s agricultural community, supporting our young people through agricultural education, investing in workforce development and ensuring critical resources are available to our beginning farmers,” said New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets Commissioner Richard A. Ball.
